# A full root-midpoint star forces an affine homothetic centroid graph

An actual convex-compatible homothetic family imposes a concrete extra identity absent from the abstract root-coefficient tree. If one root is the midpoint of an exact Minkowski pair involving **every** other root, then all root radii and centroids are affine functions of their integer bases. Every further zero-slack forest edge preserves those affine identities. The resulting entire centroid graph is an affine copy of its lattice-convex base support, so its weighted graph depth satisfies the ordinary `2^-n` bound.

In particular the 43-node abstract counterexample in `candidate 4c13e7d95b295d25` cannot survive **any** actual concave homothetic roof completion which preserves all its first-generation star equalities and its nonaffine graph. This conclusion applies to nonuniform radii as well as uniform ones. It is a theorem for the full-star subclass, not for all zero-slack forests.

## 1. Actual family and forest hypotheses

Let `C` be compact convex, and let `P` be its finite set of positive `d`-volume integer fibers, where `d>=1`. Write

    K_p=a_p+r_p K,       r_p>0,                        (1)

where `K` is a fixed full-dimensional convex body in `R^d`, translated so that its centroid is zero. Thus `a_p` is the actual centroid of `K_p`.

Suppose there are roots `v_1,...,v_J in P` and a terminating forest such that every nonroot `p` has an associated root `v_c` and parent `F(p)` satisfying

    F(p)=(p+v_c)/2,
    K_F(p)=(K_p+K_vc)/2.                              (2)

The common homothetic shape gives

    a_F(p)=(a_p+a_vc)/2,
    r_F(p)=(r_p+r_vc)/2.                              (3)

No volume-maximality or parity tie hypothesis beyond this actual terminating forest is needed for the theorem. Recursing in (2)--(3) shows that every base, centroid, and radius is the same integer affine combination of the corresponding root data. In particular

    aff(P)=aff{v_1,...,v_J}.                            (4)

Assume one designated root `p_*=v_j` has a full exact midpoint star: for every `c!=j`,

    q_c=2p_*-v_c in P,
    K_p*=(K_qc+K_vc)/2.                               (5)

These need not be designated edges of the original forest; their exact set equalities are what matter.

## 2. Supporting-plane saturation at the root

Replace `C` by the convex hull `C^+` of its positive integer fibers, and work relative to `Q=conv P` in the base. Every prescribed positive fiber is unchanged: the new hull is contained in the old body and contains the whole old fiber. Convex combinations of full-dimensional fibers show that every real fiber over `Q` has positive `d`-volume. The hull is compact and all support functions below are finite.

Put `m=dim aff P`. Equations (4)--(5) show that `p_*` is in the relative interior of `Q`: the centrally symmetric set

    conv{p_*+(v_c-p_*),p_*-(v_c-p_*):1<=c<=J}

lies in `Q` and has affine hull `aff P`. If `m=0`, the conclusions below are immediate; suppose `m>0`.

On `Q`, the function

    R(z)=(|C^+_z|/|K|)^(1/d)                          (6)

is concave by Brunn--Minkowski and satisfies `R(p)=r_p` for all `p in P`. Since `p_*` is in the relative interior, it has an affine supporting majorant `ell_r` there:

    R(z)<=ell_r(z) on Q,       R(p_*)=ell_r(p_*).        (7)

This is the elementary supporting-plane property of a finite concave function at an interior point, applied in `aff P`. It can equivalently be obtained by separating its convex hypograph from a point vertically above `(p_*,R(p_*))` and taking the supporting limit; local boundedness at an interior point makes the vertical normal coefficient nonzero.

The exact set equality in (5) implies `r_qc+r_vc=2r_p*`. Since `q_c+v_c=2p_*`, the two nonnegative majorant gaps satisfy

    [ell_r(q_c)-r_qc]+[ell_r(v_c)-r_vc]=0.

Consequently

    r_vc=ell_r(v_c) for every root c.                  (8)

The same argument works for every fixed continuous direction `u`. Convexity of `C^+` makes

    H_u(z)=h_(C^+_z)(u)                               (9)

concave on `Q`: every Minkowski interpolation of two fibers is contained in the intermediate fiber. Choose a supporting affine majorant `ell_u` at `p_*`. The exact set identity (5), now evaluated with the support function, again makes both majorant gaps vanish. Hence

    h_(K_vc)(u)=ell_u(v_c) for every root c.            (10)

This saturation step retains the actual support functions. It does not infer centroid linearity from Minkowski additivity for arbitrary shapes.

## 3. Affine root data, then the entire forest

For a homothetic fiber (1),

    h_(K_vc)(u)=u dot a_vc+r_vc h_K(u).

Combining (8)--(10),

    u dot a_vc=ell_u(v_c)-h_K(u)ell_r(v_c).             (11)

The right side is affine in the base. Apply (11) to the `d` standard coordinate directions. There is one affine map `A:aff P -> R^d` such that

    a_vc=A(v_c) for every c.                           (12)

The affine functions `A` and `ell_r` are now fixed on all roots. Recursing backward along the terminating forest using (2)--(3) gives, for **every** `p in P`,

    a_p=A(p),           r_p=ell_r(p).                  (13)

Thus the centroid graph is

    G={(p,A(p)):p in P},                               (14)

an injective affine copy of the original base set. This conclusion includes translated homothetic fibers; it is not limited to fibers centered at a common point.

## 4. The exact weighted graph-depth consequence

The positive base set `P` is lattice-convex. Indeed, if an integer `z` is a convex combination of points in `P`, the corresponding Minkowski combination of positive full-dimensional fibers has positive volume and is contained in `C_z`, so `z in P`.

Let arbitrary positive atom weights `w_p` have total `T`. The saturated lattice in `aff P`, translated by a point of `P`, is isomorphic to `Z^m`, with `m<=n`. Ordinary Doignon in that relative lattice gives a point of `P` of weighted depth at least `T/2^m`. For completeness, this application has a finite form. For each subset `E of P` with weight greater than `(1-2^-m)T`, consider `conv E`. Any `2^m` such convex hulls contain a common atom, because the union of the corresponding atom complements has total weight strictly less than `T`. Doignon therefore supplies an integer point in all these hulls. It lies in `conv P`, hence in `P`. Any closed containing halfspace of weight less than `T/2^m` would have a complementary atom set `E` of weight greater than `(1-2^-m)T`; since that finite set is strictly outside the halfspace, its convex hull excludes the chosen point, a contradiction. For `m=0` the single atom has depth `T` directly.

Under the affine embedding (14), an ambient halfspace restricts to an affine halfspace in the base, or to the whole or empty graph. It follows that some actual graph point satisfies

    inf_(H contains (p,A(p))) sum_(q:G_q in H) w_q
        >=T/2^m>=T/2^n.                              (15)

In particular (15) holds for the homothetic volume weights `w_p=|K|r_p^d`. At that graph point, every original ambient containing halfspace contains the centroid of every counted fiber; ordinary Grunbaum in each such fiber gives actual mixed cap mass at least

    Gamma_d T/2^m >= Gamma_d T/2^n.                    (16)

Equation (16) proves OC for this expressly restricted full-star homothetic forest class. It is not a count-reduction theorem for an arbitrary forest.

## 5. Why the abstract ternary tree cannot preserve its bad geometry

The 43-node tree has roots `e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3` and contains all three nodes `2e_0-e_c`, `c=1,2,3`, already at its first generation. Any actual projection of this tree preserving the graph's midpoint equations therefore has the full star (5). If its projected base rank is two, (13) forces its actual centroid graph to have affine rank at most two. The abstract coefficient graph has affine rank three, so an affine embedding of its entire three-dimensional affine span into that actual graph is impossible. Injectivity only on the finite node set would not preserve affine rank, and is not excluded by this rank statement. Separately, a realization with exactly these 43 unit-weight nodes which preserved their certified containing caps of at most seven atoms would contradict (15), because `7<43/4`. If a completion adds positive fibers, their additional weights and cap contributions must be included; the old seven-atom counts do not transfer automatically.

Changing the four root radii does not repair this obstruction: (8) forces those changed radii to be affine in their projected bases, and (13) propagates that identity through all generations. A lattice-convex roof completion may add fibers, but if it preserves the actual full-star equalities and the terminating forest hypotheses, it still satisfies (15). Therefore the abstract counter cannot simply be promoted to an actual counter by filling missing integer bases and choosing a nonuniform concave roof.

This identifies the additional geometric constraint exactly: one common supporting majorant at an actual positive fiber simultaneously saturates the full root star. The abstract coefficient conditions do not impose that common support-plane relation.
